chapter.title: The Basics
chapter.summary: Barry Harris establishes the foundational pedagogical principle that technique must serve musical context, introduces the 'up and down' scale as the basic unit of practice, defines the three important arpeggios on the dominant 7th, explains the pivoting technique, and presents the half-step practice model as the generative engine of bebop improvisation across dominant 7th, major, and minor (ascending melodic) scales. The chapter concludes with the practical rule of thumb for locating the related diminished chord a major 3rd above any dominant root.

sections.title: Technique vs. Musical Context
sections.summary: Harris asserts that technique is a prerequisite for jazz improvisation but must always be practiced within a musical context.

engine_rules.name: Technique requires musical context

then.voicing.quality: always embed technical exercise within a musical phrase or progression

engine_rules.preference: Never practice technique in isolation from musical meaning
engine_rules.falsifier: An exercise drill that cycles fingerings or scales with no reference to chord changes or rhythmic feel would violate this rule.
engine_rules.anchor: practice your playing—not your practicing

paragraphs.summary: Technique is a means to an end; it must always have musical context in practice.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor:
technique must always have
a musical context

sections.title: Re-creating the Rhythm Section in Practice
sections.summary: Solo practice must mentally simulate the full rhythm section at tempo.

engine_rules.name: Mental rhythm section simulation during solo practice

then.voicing.quality: maintain internal awareness of drums, bass, and chord changes at tempo

engine_rules.preference: Always practice in tempo with an imagined rhythm section
engine_rules.falsifier: Practicing scales freely with no tempo and no internal harmonic reference would violate this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
it is essential to re-create the rhythm section for yourself as
you play. Hear the drums, the bass and the chord changes.

sections.title: 'Up and Down' Scale Definition
sections.summary: The 'up and down' scale is a 2-bar phrase played from the tonic up to the 7th degree and back.

engine_rules.name: Up-and-down scale as 2-bar phrase unit

then.voicing.shape: ascend from tonic to 7th degree, then descend straight back to tonic, producing a 2-bar phrase

engine_rules.preference: The 'up and down' form is the standard scale exercise unit
engine_rules.falsifier: A scale exercise that ascends a full octave (tonic to octave) rather than stopping at the 7th would not be an 'up and down' in Harris's sense.
engine_rules.anchor:
a scale played from its tonic up to its 7th
degree

sections.title: Three Important Arpeggios on Dominant 7th
sections.summary: Only three arpeggios on the dominant 7th scale are designated 'important': on the tonic, 5th, and 7th degrees.

engine_rules.name: Three important arpeggios on dominant 7th scale

then.voicing.shape: prioritize arpeggios built on scale degrees 1, 5, and 7

engine_rules.preference: On a C dominant 7th, practice the arpeggios rooted on C, G, and Bb
engine_rules.falsifier: Treating an arpeggio built on the 2nd or 4th degree of the dominant 7th scale as equally important would contradict this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
The three important arpeggios on the dominant 7th scale are found
on the tonic, the Sth and the 7th.

sections.title: Pivoting Technique Definition
sections.summary: Pivoting creates new highest/lowest notes that feel rhythmically stronger, altering accentual structure.

engine_rules.name: Pivoting creates rhythmic emphasis at new range extremes

then.voicing.shape: insert pivot point to create new highest or lowest note, generating natural rhythmic accent

engine_rules.preference: Use pivoting when a melodic line would otherwise exceed instrumental range or when rhythmic reaccentuation is desired
engine_rules.falsifier: A straight ascending or descending line with no pivot is unrelated; the rule is non-vacuous only when a pivot is inserted.
engine_rules.anchor:
the accentual structure of the line changes where the pivot creates new
highest and lowest notes, which naturally feel rhythmically stronger

sections.title: Half-Step Practice Model Definition
sections.summary: Half-steps are added to the descending form of the scale; each scale type has its own rules.

engine_rules.name: Half-steps added to descending scale form per scale-type rules
engine_rules.preference: Half-steps appear in the descending form only; each scale type has its own rule set
engine_rules.falsifier: Adding half-steps to the ascending form of the scale, or applying dominant 7th half-step placements to the major scale, would violate this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
In their basic role, they appear as notes added to the
descending form of the scale.

sections.title: Major Scale Half-Step Rules
sections.summary: Four rules govern half-step insertion in the major scale by starting-degree group.

engine_rules.name: Major Rule 1 (1-3-5-maj7): one half-step between 6 and 5
engine_rules.falsifier: Inserting a half-step between 2 and 1 instead of 6 and 5 when descending from scale degree 1 violates Rule 1.
engine_rules.anchor:
The first rule for descending from the 1-3-5 and major7 is: 1
added half-step between the 6-5.

engine_rules.name: Major Rule 2 (3-5-maj7): three half-steps
engine_rules.falsifier: Using only one or two half-steps when applying Rule 2 to the 3-5-maj7 group would be incomplete.
engine_rules.anchor:
The second rule applying to the 3-5 and major7 is: 3 added half-
steps between the 3-2; 2-1; 6-5.

engine_rules.name: Major Rule 1 (2-4-6): no added half-steps
engine_rules.falsifier: Adding any half-step when applying Rule 1 from scale degree 2, 4, or 6 violates this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
The first rule for descending from the 2-4-6 is: no added half-
steps.

engine_rules.name: Major Rule 2 (2-4-6): two half-steps
engine_rules.falsifier: Using three half-steps (as in Rule 2 for 1-3-5-maj7) when applying Rule 2 to the 2-4-6 group violates this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
The second rule for the 2-4-6 is: 2 added half-steps which can
come between the 2-1; 6-5 or between the major7-6; 6-5.

sections.title: Minor Scale Half-Step Rules
sections.summary: Use ascending melodic minor; major scale rules apply except where they would insert a b3 — substitute any other note.

engine_rules.name: Minor half-step rules use ascending melodic minor

then.scale.insert_half_step_at: same positions as major rules applied to ascending melodic minor (1-2-b3-4-5-6-maj7)

engine_rules.preference: Use ascending melodic minor, never natural or harmonic minor, as the base
engine_rules.falsifier: Applying Harris half-step rules to a natural minor scale instead of ascending melodic minor would violate this rule.
engine_rules.anchor:
The minor scale that the half-steps are added to is the melodic minor in
ascending form-tonic - 2 - b3 - 4 - 5 - 6 - major7.

engine_rules.name: Minor scale b3 exception: substitute any note for b3 insertion

then.scale.insert_half_step_at: any note other than b3 (already present); alternatively use interval jump or repeat the same note twice

engine_rules.preference: b3 is the single exception; all other placements identical to major
engine_rules.falsifier: Inserting an additional b3 via the half-step rule in ascending melodic minor would be redundant and contradicts the exception.
engine_rules.anchor:
The one exception to this is where
the major scale rules add a b3rd. Because this note is already present in
the melodic minor scale, any other note may be used in its place.

sections.title: Finding the Related Diminished Chord
sections.summary: Build the related diminished chord a major 3rd above the dominant root.

engine_rules.name: Related diminished is built a major 3rd above the dominant 7th root

then.chord_symbol.substitute: diminished chord built on the note a major 3rd above the dominant 7th root

engine_rules.preference: For any dominant 7th, go up a major 3rd from the root
engine_rules.falsifier: Building the related diminished a minor 3rd above the dominant root (e.g., Eb° for C7) would not yield the Harris related diminished.
engine_rules.anchor:
The rule of thumb for finding a related diminished chord is to
build it a major 3rd above the dominant note.

chapter.title: Applications
chapter.summary: Chapter 2 teaches the Three-Step Solo Building method and introduces three load-bearing harmonic definitions: Related Diminished Chord (major 3rd above the dominant), Important Minor (the minor 7th on the 5th of a dominant 7th scale, i.e. V/V), and the Minor 6 Diminished Scale (minor 6 + its related diminished).

sections.title: Three-Step Solo Building
sections.summary: Choose correct scale(s) → make many phrases in all keys & tempos → port phrases to other tunes using same progression.

engine_rules.name: Scale selection must precede phrase generation

then.scale.type: scale(s) that outline the chord progression

engine_rules.falsifier: Playing phrases that do not derive from a scale outlining the progression (e.g., lydian phrase over a plain dominant V where mixolydian is required) violates step 1.
engine_rules.anchor:
Choose the correct scale(s) to outline the chord
progression (song). Practice the scale(s) thoroughly.

engine_rules.name: Practice scale-derived phrases in all keys and challenging tempos
engine_rules.falsifier: Practicing a phrase only in C and never transposing violates the all-keys requirement.
engine_rules.anchor:
Make-up as many different phrases as possible
based on the scale(s) outlining the harmony, Practice
them in all keys, and at challenging tempos.

engine_rules.name: Transfer phrases across tunes sharing the same progression
engine_rules.falsifier: Treating a II-V-I phrase as tune-specific and never reusing it across other II-V-I tunes violates step 3.
engine_rules.anchor:
Find different tunes that make use of the chord
progression that you are working on, and try out the
phrases in each of them.

sections.title: Related Diminished Chord Definition
sections.summary: Built a major 3rd above the dominant note. In D major, A → C# (C# diminished).

engine_rules.name: Build related diminished a major 3rd above the dominant

then.chord_symbol.substitute: diminished7 chord rooted a major 3rd above the dominant note

engine_rules.falsifier: Building the diminished a minor 3rd above (B° in key of D rather than C#°) is the standard vii°/V, not the Harris related diminished.
engine_rules.anchor:
The related diminished chord is built from a major 3rd above the domi-
nant note, For instance, in the key of D the dominant note is A anda
third above is C#.

sections.title: Important Minor Definition
sections.summary: The chord on the 5th degree of a dominant 7th scale — the 'five of five' (V/V).

engine_rules.name: Important Minor = minor 7 on scale degree 5 of a dominant

then.chord_symbol.substitute: minor7 chord rooted on the 5th degree of the dominant 7th scale (V/V)

engine_rules.falsifier: Labeling the chord on the 4th degree (IVm7) as 'important minor' violates this definition; it must be on the 5th degree.
engine_rules.anchor:
"Important minor' is the term given to the chord found on the Sth
degree of a dominant 7th scale (5 of 5),

sections.title: Minor 6 Diminished Scale Definition
sections.summary: Combine minor 6 chord with its related diminished (a major 3rd above the dominant note of the scale).

engine_rules.name: Minor 6 Diminished Scale = Minor 6 + Related Diminished

then.scale.insert_half_step_at: diminished chord tones built a major 3rd above the dominant note of the scale, merged with the minor 6 chord tones

engine_rules.falsifier: Building with a minor 7 chord (Cm7 + B°) instead of minor 6 does not yield the Harris Minor 6 Diminished Scale.
engine_rules.anchor:
This scale is formed by combining a minor 6 chord with its related
diminished chord, The diminished chord is built from a major 3rd
above the dominant note of the scale.

chapter.title: Movable Chords for Piano and Guitar
chapter.summary: Harris introduces the 'scale for chording' concept, assigns virtually all chords to the major 6 diminished or minor 6 diminished scale, articulates two axiomatic equivalences (m7 = inverted M6, m7b5 = inverted m6), exposes the C6 diminished scale as three interlocking diminished chords, and supplies the single mechanical voicing rule: move each note to the next note of the scale.
key_phrases: move each note to the next note of the scale

sections.title: Scale for Chording Concept
sections.summary: Two scales — major 6 diminished and minor 6 diminished — absorb virtually any chord.

engine_rules.name: Assign any chord to major-6-dim or minor-6-dim
engine_rules.falsifier: A chord that cannot be mapped to either 6-diminished scale would refute the universality claim (Harris asserts none exists in standard jazz vocabulary).
engine_rules.anchor: a 'scale for chording,' and a method of assigning virtually any chord to one of two scales—the major 6 diminished and the minor 6 diminished.

sections.title: Harmonic Rigidity Misconception
sections.summary: Treating chords as fixed vertical points causes players to repeat two or three voicings per chord symbol.

engine_rules.name: Reject fixed-voicing repetition for a single chord change

then.voicing.shape: apply scale-based movement to generate alternative voicings

engine_rules.falsifier: A pedal-tone ostinato that intentionally repeats a single voicing for expressive effect would not be refuted by this rule (intent matters).
engine_rules.anchor: The misconception that chords are fixed points in the tune, bound by vertical harmonic movement, may be the culprit behind the tendency to play the same two or three voicings over and over for the same change.

sections.title: C6 Diminished Scale Construction
sections.summary: Eight notes of C6 diminished decompose into three diminished chords: {C,A}, {E,G}, and B diminished (B,D,F,Ab).

engine_rules.name: C6 Diminished Scale = three interlocking diminished chords

then.voicing.quality: partition scale tones into three diminished-chord groups: {C,A}, {E,G}, and B-diminished {B,D,F,Ab}

engine_rules.falsifier: If any scale tone cannot be assigned to one of the three diminished chords, the decomposition fails (all 8 tones are accounted for in Harris's claim).
engine_rules.anchor: This scale is actually comprised of all 3 diminished chords. The C and A belong to one diminished, the E and G to a second, and the B diminished chord provides the other four notes of the scale.

engine_rules.name: Related dominant substitution via shared diminished triad

then.chord_symbol.substitute: any of the four dominant 7 chords sharing the same diminished triad are interchangeable

engine_rules.falsifier: A dominant substitute that does NOT share a common diminished triad with the target (e.g., E7 substituted for D7 — different diminished families) is not licensed by this rule.
engine_rules.anchor: The C and A belong to one diminished, the E and G to a second, and the B diminished chord provides the other four notes of the scale.

sections.title: m7 and m7b5 Re-thinking
sections.summary: m7 = inversion of a major 6 chord; m7b5 = inversion of a minor 6 chord. Collapses four chord families into the two 6-diminished scales.

engine_rules.name: m7 chord is an inversion of a major 6 chord

then.chord_symbol.substitute: major6 chord rooted a minor third above the m7 root (e.g., Dm7 = F6/D)

engine_rules.falsifier: A minor 7 spelling that cannot be rewritten as an inversion of a major 6 chord would falsify the equivalence; no such spelling exists in 12-TET.
engine_rules.anchor: Every minor 7 chord is an inversion of a major 6th chord, and every minor? flat5 chord is an inversion of a minor 6th chord.

engine_rules.name: m7b5 chord is an inversion of a minor 6 chord

then.chord_symbol.substitute: minor6 chord rooted a minor third above the m7b5 root (e.g., Bm7b5 = Dm6/B)

engine_rules.falsifier: A half-diminished spelling that cannot be rewritten as an inversion of a minor 6 chord would falsify the equivalence; no such spelling exists in 12-TET.
engine_rules.anchor: Every minor 7 chord is an inversion of a major 6th chord, and every minor? flat5 chord is an inversion of a minor 6th chord.

sections.title: Moving Voicing Rule
sections.summary: Every voice moves to the adjacent note of the governing 6-diminished scale.

engine_rules.name: Move every voice to the adjacent scale degree

then.voicing.shape: displace each chord tone to the immediately adjacent note (up or down) in the governing 6-diminished scale

engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing movement that skips a scale degree (moves by a whole step when a scale-internal half step is available) violates this rule — e.g., C to E bypassing D in C6 diminished.
engine_rules.anchor: Remember to move each note to the next note of the scale.

chapter.title: The Rhythm Section
chapter.summary: Chapter 4 establishes the related dominant 7th substitution: dominants drawn from the same diminished triad are interchangeable at V7→I. Worked out via the D7→Gmaj7 / F#-diminished family, the major-minor-minor/6 voice-leading move, and a generalized Stella by Starlight Roman-numeral formula.

sections.title: Related Dominant 7th Substitutions
sections.summary: Dominants sharing a common diminished triad substitute for one another at V7→I.

engine_rules.name: Related dominant 7 substitution at V7→I

then.chord_symbol.substitute: any of the four dominants sharing the same diminished triad

engine_rules.falsifier: A dominant that does NOT share the same diminished triad as the V7 (e.g., E7 in place of D7→Gmaj7, since E7 derives from G#-diminished, not F#-diminished) is not a valid related-dominant substitute.
engine_rules.anchor: we have illustrations of how related dominant 7th chords may be used to substitute 'for eachother' when the V7 chord moves back to the I.

sections.title: D7–Gmaj7 Substitution Example
sections.summary: F#-diminished (F#–A–C–Eb) generates D7, F7, Ab7, B7 — any voiced over D bass.

engine_rules.name: F#-diminished family: D7 / F7 / Ab7 / B7 over D bass
engine_rules.falsifier: Using E7 or Bb7 over a D bass when resolving to Gmaj7 — neither derives from F#-diminished, so neither qualifies as a related dominant in this family.
engine_rules.anchor: D7 going to G major is outlined. The diminished that D7 comes from is F# (F#-A-C-Eb). Given that F7, Ab7, and B7 are also related to F# diminished, they make very interesting voicings when played against D in the bass.

engine_rules.name: Maintain bass root while substituting related dominant upper structure
engine_rules.falsifier: Moving the bass to the root of the substitute (e.g., F in bass for F7 instead of D) dissolves the bass-continuity effect Harris identifies.
engine_rules.anchor: they make very interesting voicings when played against D in the bass.

sections.title: Major-Minor-Minor/6 Voice-Leading Move
sections.summary: Bb major → G minor → Gm/E: the 6th degree of the minor chord placed in the bass.

engine_rules.name: Major → Minor → Minor/6 three-chord voice-leading unit
engine_rules.falsifier: Placing the 5th in the bass on the third chord (Gm/D instead of Gm/E) breaks the specific bass-line formula Harris names.
engine_rules.anchor: This figure shows the progression from major to minor to minor with the 6th degree in the bass:(Bb major-G minor-Gm/E).

sections.title: Stella by Starlight Harmonic Formula
sections.summary: Generalized Roman-numeral template: I – III7 – relative minor – bVIdim – Imaj/5 – minor/6.

engine_rules.name: Stella by Starlight generalized harmonic sequence
engine_rules.falsifier: Substituting IVmaj7 for bVIdim removes the diminished-color pivot Harris identifies as structural; the bVIdim is not freely replaceable.
engine_rules.anchor: The chord movements are I major- IlI7-relative minor-bVIdim-Imaj/5-minor/6.

chapter.title: Vocalizing
chapter.summary: Grounds vocal jazz in independent time/phrasing and scalar-rhythmical mastery, then applies key-specific diminished-chord substitution (E-dim for C7 in F minor; B-dim for G7 in C minor), defines the augmented arpeggio (major arpeggio with raised 5th), and the whole-tone scale (six notes, all whole-steps from the root).

sections.title: Vocalist's Role and Independence
sections.summary: Singer is storyteller and rhythmic instrument; must develop time/phrasing independent of the rhythm section.

engine_rules.name: Singer must internalize time independent of rhythm section
engine_rules.falsifier: A singer who locks mechanically to the drummer's pulse on every downbeat, never anticipating or displacing, violates this rule even if rhythmically accurate.
engine_rules.anchor: it is essential for the singer to develop a sense of time and phrasing independent of what the rhythm section lays down.

sections.title: Technical Skills as Prerequisite to Improvisation
sections.summary: Scalar and rhythmical technical mastery is the gate that unlocks nuanced improvisation.

engine_rules.name: Scalar and rhythmical mastery is prerequisite to expressive improvisation
engine_rules.falsifier: Jumping to expressive phrasing without drilling scales and rhythmic subdivisions — producing nuance that cannot be reproduced on demand — violates this rule.
engine_rules.anchor: It is also vital for the vocalist, as it is for any instrumentalist in this music, to develop technical (scalar and rhythmical) skills in order to master the art of improvisation

sections.title: Key-Specific Diminished Chord Substitution
sections.summary: C7 in F minor → E-diminished; G7 in C minor → B-diminished.

engine_rules.name: C7 in F minor: substitute E-diminished
engine_rules.falsifier: Using B-diminished over C7 in F minor violates this rule; B-diminished is reserved for G7 in C minor.
engine_rules.anchor: C7 (in the key of F minor) uses the E-diminished chord; while G7 (in the key of C minor) uses the B diminished chord.

engine_rules.name: G7 in C minor: substitute B-diminished
engine_rules.falsifier: Using E-diminished over G7 in C minor violates this rule; E-diminished is reserved for C7 in F minor.
engine_rules.anchor: C7 (in the key of F minor) uses the E-diminished chord; while G7 (in the key of C minor) uses the B diminished chord.

engine_rules.name: In minor-key dominants, related diminished sits a major 3rd above the dominant root

then.chord_symbol.substitute: diminished chord built a major 3rd above the dominant 7 root

engine_rules.falsifier: Choosing a diminished a tritone or minor-third away from the dominant root (rather than a major 3rd above) does not produce the Harris related-diminished substitution. (E.g., for C7, F#° instead of E°.)
engine_rules.anchor: C7 (in the key of F minor) uses the E-diminished chord; while G7 (in the key of C minor) uses the B diminished chord.

sections.title: Augmented Arpeggio Definition
sections.summary: Major arpeggio with the 5th degree raised a half-step.

engine_rules.name: Augmented arpeggio = major arpeggio with 5th raised a half-step
engine_rules.falsifier: Playing a major arpeggio without raising the 5th, or raising the 4th instead, does not constitute an augmented arpeggio under Harris's definition.
engine_rules.anchor: An Ab augmented arpeggio (the 5th degree is raised a half-step from the major)

sections.title: Whole Tone Scale Definition
sections.summary: Six-note scale built on whole steps from the root.

engine_rules.name: Whole tone scale = six-note scale built on consecutive whole-steps from the root
engine_rules.falsifier: A seven-note scale, or one containing any half-step interval anywhere in the series, is not a whole tone scale under Harris's definition.
engine_rules.anchor: The Ab whole tone scale (a six note scale built on whole-steps above the root)
